plain: Able to be raised in court as a claim or defense

webster.text: That may be pleaded; that may be alleged in proof, defense or vindication; as a right or privilege pleadable at law.

example.quote: He shall have power to grant reprieves and pardons; but his pardon shall not be pleadable in bar of an impeachment.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, August 6, 1787
